samples.title: Producer-consumer
samples.summary: Two producers and two consumers share a bounded queue of three jobs.
watch: Producers wait when the queue is full
Consumers wait when it is empty
Each job can be followed from put to get to work

samples.title: Bounded queue backpressure
samples.summary: A fast producer, a slow consumer and a queue that holds only two items.
watch: The producer blocks on put until the consumer makes room
Queue depth sits at its limit while the consumer works

samples.title: Item lineage
samples.summary: Pages are split into sentences and sentences into word counts; every new item records which item it came from.
watch: Open the Lineage tab and pick any item
Walk from a word count back to the page it came from
Click an item to jump to the moment it was created

samples.title: Cancellation and shutdown
samples.summary: An immediate queue shutdown discards pending jobs and stops two workers.
watch: Queued jobs are discarded, not processed
Jobs already in progress still finish

samples.title: Plain program, threads only
samples.summary: An ordinary program with no Concurim imports, recorded at the threads level.
watch: Threads and their lifetimes are visible
The queue is not observed, and the viewer says so

samples.title: Plain program, threads and queues
samples.summary: The same program recorded with automatic queue instrumentation.
watch: Compare with the previous example: same code, more visible
Queue contents appear without changing the program

samples.title: Lock contention
samples.summary: Four threads take turns inside one lock-protected critical section.
watch: Only one thread holds the lock at a time
The others wait, and the timeline shows each wait and hold

samples.title: Lock ordering (wait cycle)
samples.summary: Two threads take two locks in opposite order and wait for each other until a timeout ends the standoff.
watch: Open the Resources view to see who holds and who waits
Each thread holds the lock the other one wants
Both waits end with a timeout, not a result

samples.title: Semaphore limit
samples.summary: A semaphore with two permits lets only two of five threads work at once.
watch: Permits drop to zero while two threads work
Waiting threads resume as permits are released

samples.title: threading.Event
samples.summary: Three runners wait at a gate until the starter sets an event; a later timed wait gives up.
watch: Waiting threads block until the event is set, then continue on their own schedule
A timed wait on an unset event times out

samples.title: threading.Barrier
samples.summary: Three workers arrive at a barrier. The first two wait; the third releases all of them together.
watch: The first arrivals wait; the last one releases everyone together
Nobody continues until all three have arrived

samples.title: threading.Condition
samples.summary: Two readers sleep on a condition; a poster adds messages and notifies.
watch: notify() does not release the lock: the poster still holds it
A woken reader must re-acquire the lock before it continues

samples.title: ThreadPoolExecutor
samples.summary: Six tasks run on two pool workers; one task fails.
watch: Tasks wait in the pool's queue, then move to a worker
The failing task is marked failed; the pool keeps going

samples.title: CPU-bound threads (compare builds)
samples.summary: Four pool threads count primes. Record it under a standard and a free-threaded Python, then compare the two.
watch: On a standard build the tasks take turns running Python code
Use Compare to put two recordings on one time scale
The viewer shows task start and end, never GIL ownership

samples.title: Future cancel, callbacks and as_completed
samples.summary: Four tasks on two workers: one queued task is cancelled, a callback runs on a worker, and results come back in completion order.
watch: A cancelled task leaves the queue and never starts
The callback runs on the worker thread that finished the task
as_completed returns tasks in the order they finish

samples.title: ProcessPoolExecutor
samples.summary: Eight CPU-bound tasks run in three worker processes.
watch: Each worker is a separate process, drawn like a thread
Tasks move from the pool's queue to a worker and back out when done

samples.title: multiprocessing.Pool
samples.summary: Pool.map sends six items to two worker processes; each item is one task.
watch: Each item is a task that waits in the pool, runs in a worker process and returns a copy of its result
Click a task submission to see how big its copied argument was

samples.title: Process: copied vs shared
samples.summary: Three child processes get a list (copied) and a counter (shared); only the counter changes for the parent.
watch: The start request says which argument is copied and which is shared
Each child is its own process with its own memory

samples.title: Asyncio task switching
samples.summary: Three tasks share one thread; the event loop switches between them.
watch: Exactly one task runs at a time
A task that awaits is suspended, not blocked

samples.title: asyncio.TaskGroup
samples.summary: Three tasks share one async-with block. One fails, so the group cancels the others and raises an ExceptionGroup.
watch: The parent waits at the end of the block until every task ends
A failing task cancels its siblings
The errors are raised together as one group

samples.title: asyncio.Queue
samples.summary: One producer task and two consumer tasks share a queue of two items.
watch: A full queue suspends only the producer task
Consumers wait on an empty queue while others run

samples.title: asyncio.Condition
samples.summary: Two tasks wait for a counter to reach a target; a ticker notifies them after each tick.
watch: Waiting tasks are suspended, not blocked, while others run
A notified task re-acquires the lock and re-checks its predicate
